maritime.title: Maritime SF
maritime.seoDescription: A free San Francisco walking tour of the Crissy Field waterfront, led by Eric Friedman of San Francisco City Guides. Maritime history, the living bay, and the stories behind Golden Gate.

meetAt.description: This tour meets at the Crissy Field East Beach at the picnic tables by the changing rooms in the parking lot, not the picnic tables east of the parking lot. I arrive 15 minutes early — please join me!
meetAt.transit: MUNI 30 to Broderick St & Jefferson St. Or take the free Presidio GO shuttle — exit at the Presidio Community YMCA and walk down the hill, or continue to the Presidio Visitor Center for a bite to eat and a great view before walking to meet us.

maritime.endAt: Picnic tables closer to the marina

japantown.title: Japantown
japantown.seoDescription: A free walking tour of San Francisco's Japantown — one of only three remaining in the US — led by Eric Friedman of San Francisco City Guides. Three hidden histories, food culture, and surprising crossovers.

japaneseteagarden.title: Japanese Tea Garden
japaneseteagarden.seoDescription: A free walking tour of the Japanese Tea Garden in Golden Gate Park, led by Eric Friedman of San Francisco City Guides. Over 130 years of artistry, horticulture, and history in the oldest public Japanese garden outside Japan.

eventLocation.name: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park

admission.note: The Garden charges admission for most visitors. San Francisco residents and certain other groups receive free admission at any time; others receive free admission before 10:00 AM on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Either way, timed entry tickets are now required for everyone — free or paid. This is separate from our tour, which is free with an optional donation requested.
admission.ticketsNote: Purchase a timed ticket (free or paid, depending on your status) for the hour before the tour starts — e.g., a noon ticket for a 1:00 PM tour — so you can enter on time.
admission.comboNote: Combination tickets covering the Japanese Tea Garden, the Botanical Garden, and the Conservatory of Flowers are available at a discount — a great option if you plan to visit more than one.

meetAt.description: Meet inside the gate, immediately past the kiosk, by the azaleas. I arrive 15 minutes early — please join me! Look for me: 6'1", in a red City Guides jacket.
meetAt.transit: MUNI N to 9th Avenue, 5/5R to 8th Avenue, or 44 to the park — check transit apps for more options

parking.note: Allow plenty of time to find street parking on Martin Luther King Jr Drive. Alternatively, the paid garage under the Music Concourse has two entrances: one on the south side and one on the north side (typically less congested).

details.climbing: Some up/down, stairs, and uneven paths — sturdy shoes advised
details.climate: Can be cool but not windy inside the garden. Layers recommended!
details.ageRange: Children of any age who like to learn, can listen to stories, and maybe even help out are welcome!

restrooms.before: Turn right after the kiosk and proceed to the building by the bamboo

forKids.description: Nature Quest is a fun visual scavenger hunt that we hope will enhance your visit to the Garden. Please remember to look, not touch.

foodShopping.note: 9th Avenue, a short walk from the Garden, is a local foodie destination worth exploring, but the Tea House is your best option!

entries.description: Linda H. on the botany of tea, then beverage preparation and recommendations for the Tea House menu — in two parts. Read this before you come to get an idea of what you'd like to try!

links.label: Part two: preparation & the Tea House

entries.description: Eric F. filmed traditional fortune cracker production in Kyōto — the original molds are on display right here in the Gift Shop. The video traces the connections between Kyōto, San Francisco's Japanese American community, and a treat the world now thinks of as Chinese. The Court of Historical Review Wikipedia entry describes the 1983 case in which it determined that the fortune cookie as we know it was invented right here in the Tea Garden.
Eric F. on the botany and horticulture of Japanese Maples, with references for those who want to go deeper.

entries.topic: Brackets in the Bell Tower Gate
entries.description: Eric F. built a working scale model of the roof-support brackets from the Bell Tower Gate — a marvel of traditional joinery engineering. The project was featured in the newsletter of Kezuroukai, a North American hand-tool woodworking organization.

entries.sectionDescription: The world's oldest continuously operating public Japanese garden outside of Japan reflects the designs and aesthetics of many contributors. Here are some that have been treated in our newsletter.

entries.description: Philip S. traces the remarkable story of the young George Turner Marsh — from Yokohama to America, and ultimately to the Japanese Village that became this Garden — in a three-part historical essay.

Philip S. examines how Samuel Newsom Jr. helped guide the Japanese Tea Garden through the difficult postwar years — preserving trees, reshaping landscapes, and drawing on years spent studying in Japan to reconnect the Garden with Japanese design traditions after wartime rupture. His work around the waterfall and dwarf tree collection reflects a broader effort to restore continuity, memory, and cultural dignity to one of San Francisco's most significant historic spaces.

Eric F. chronicles the story of how Imperial Palace landscape architect Nagao Sakurai helped shape the Japanese Tea Garden into a living work of postwar reconciliation — bringing centuries of Japanese garden tradition into conversation with San Francisco through designs that were subtle, rooted in but not limited by tradition, and meant to be experienced rather than merely viewed. His 1953 dry landscape garden behind the pagoda remains one of the Garden's clearest expressions of peace, translation, and cultural continuity.

1840s.seoDescription: A free San Francisco walking tour tracing America's first Black millionaire and the city's forgotten origins, led by Eric Friedman of San Francisco City Guides and author of The Ledger and the Mirror.
